list.heading: Applications
list.intro: An application is a bot: a program that joins guilds and talks in them through Voicaw's bot API, which works like Discord's.
list.empty: You haven't made any applications yet.

create.title: New application
create.hint: Its bot will have this name too. You can change it later.

oauth2.intro: Let people log in to your website with their Voicaw account ("Login with Voicaw"). It works like Discord's OAuth2: send them to the authorise link, then trade the code for a token with your client secret. The only scope is identify: their id, username, display name and picture.
oauth2.secretHint: Your website's server uses it to trade codes for tokens. Keep it secret, and never put it in a web page or an app. Voicaw only shows it once.
oauth2.secretNew: Here's your client secret. Copy it now: it won't be shown again.
oauth2.confirmReset: The old secret stops working at once: your website can't log anyone in until it uses the new one. People already logged in stay logged in.
oauth2.redirectsHint: The exact addresses people may be sent back to after logging in (https, or http://localhost for testing). Up to {{count}}.
oauth2.noRedirects: There are no redirects yet: nobody can log in to your website until you add one.
oauth2.linkHint: Add a state parameter of your own, and check it when people come back.

general.pictureTooBig: That picture is too big (8 MB at most).
general.descriptionHint: Shown on the bot's profile and when someone adds it.
general.deleteHint: Its bot leaves every guild and its token stops working. Its messages stay.
general.confirmDelete: This can't be undone. Its bot leaves every guild it's in.

bot.tokenHint: Your bot logs in with its token. Keep it secret: anyone who has it can act as your bot. Voicaw only shows it once.
bot.tokenNew: Here's your bot's token. Copy it now: it won't be shown again.
bot.tokenWarning: Never share it or put it in code you publish. If it gets out, reset it.
bot.confirmReset: The old token stops working at once, and your bot is disconnected until it uses the new one.
bot.publicHint: Anyone with its invite link can add it to a guild they manage. When off, only you can.

install.intro: Choose what your bot may do, then share the link. Whoever adds it picks a guild where they have Manage Guild, and can only give it permissions they have themselves.
install.noGuilds: It isn't in any guilds yet.

authorize.title: Add a bot
authorize.unknown: This bot doesn't exist, or its maker hasn't made it public.
authorize.missingClient: This link doesn't say which bot to add.
authorize.noGuilds: You don't manage any guilds it isn't in already. You need Manage Guild to add a bot.
authorize.noPermissions: It doesn't ask for any permissions.
authorize.cantGrant: You don't have this permission there, so you can't give it.
authorize.notice: The bot can read and send messages in the channels it can see. Bots can't use direct messages: those are end-to-end encrypted.

login.title: Log in with Voicaw
login.wantsAccess: {{app}} wants to use your Voicaw account

scopes.identify: Know your username, display name and profile picture

login.cannot: It can't read your messages, see your guilds or act as you.
login.redirect: Once you authorise, you'll go to {{host}}.
login.privacy: What {{app}} does with this is up to its maker, not Voicaw. You can take its access away in Settings → Authorised apps.
